attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter. It is his arithmetic on figures from a deck he says he viewed.

semantics.note: 29,000 monthly hours divided by about 1,500 engineers is roughly 19 hours a month each. The proposition keeps the monthly basis and the attribution to LLM code.

contract.note: The speaker never named the deck's measurement month. Picking April 2026 is the evaluator's own assumption, and the flags say so. The reading of extra review hours as an average is fair.

evidence.note: Zillow's March 2026 remarks say it ships 40% more code per engineer. That measures output, not review hours, and covers a different period, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no authenticated copy of the deck, no check of the 29,000 hours or the 1,500 headcount, and no baseline or attribution to LLM code. The only item measures code output in a different month. The evidence neither confirms nor refutes the 19-hour average.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the $800B figure unhedged and keeps 'I estimate' on the operational share, as the source does.

contract.note: The result depends on unsupplied choices: three or four companies, what 'in the hole' means, and the start of the investment window. The contract flags all of these and its readings are ordinary.

evidence.note: Alphabet's Q1 2026 10-Q gives company-wide balances for assets in service and not yet in service. These are not the AI investment pool across four companies, so they cannot settle the claimed operational share.

reviews.rationale: There is no reconciled AI investment total for the named companies and no commissioning inventory dollar-weighted to the same pool. The one filing covers a single company, all its assets and a different basis. Neither the $800B total nor the under-half operational share is established or refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the $330B cloud figure, the estimated xAI and CoreWeave components, the four-year window and the $380B total.

contract.note: Assessing the commitments that existed at publication over a four-year window is a fair reading. The ban on squeezing longer contracts into four years without evidence is reasonable.

evidence.note: Reports a five-year Google term and a ten-year AWS term. This hints the full $300B may not fall within four years, but it gives no payment schedule.
Anthropic's own disclosure confirms the $30B Azure commitment but gives no payment timing.
Confirms the CoreWeave agreement but gives no dollar value, so the $30B estimate is unverified.

Reported terms of $1.25B a month to 2029 point to more than the $5B-a-year estimate. But either side can cancel on 90 days' notice, so the deal is potential revenue, not a fixed obligation, and the component was hedged.

reviews.rationale: No payment schedule exists for the five providers within the window. The Google and AWS terms run longer than four years, but how payments are timed is unknown. The xAI deal could cost more but is cancellable, and the CoreWeave value is undisclosed. The contract demands a complete schedule to decide, so neither support nor contradiction is established.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the hedge 'I think it's fair to assume', and the drafter set the modality to 'likely'. This is graded, qualified confidence, not a firm commitment.

contract.note: The contract scores hedged language as if it were firm. Its plain-reading rule only covers firm language. It also adds a non-compute scope the speaker never stated, and that choice decides the result.

evidence.note: The S-1, filed 2026-10-26 before the evaluation date, expects personnel costs to rise. That is a qualitative expectation with no cumulative non-compute total.

reviews.rationale: 'I think it's fair to assume' is a qualified assumption, not a firm forecast, so policy says it is not scored. In any case the window runs to May 2030 and no early crossing of the threshold is documented.
